Great was the grace of Timothy. When Barnabas departed, he finds another, equivalent to him. Barclay says loyalty to the gospel was bound to bring trouble, here by being loyal to a man treated as a criminal, and he draws out the glory of the gospel as one of power, of God's own call and plan, and of life that conquers death.

Says Paul knew Timothy needed strength and endurance, and that the strength is found in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.

The young sailor at sea is inspired with great confidence, if the Master of the ship has been preserved in a shipwreck. Says a good soldier expects hardship and does not quit when it comes, and does not tangle himself in civilian affairs because he wants to please the one who enlisted him.
A Good Soldier of Jesus Christ

"Thou therefore endure hardness as a good soldier of Jesus Christ." Oh, how great a dignity is this, to be a soldier of Jesus Christ! Observe the kings on earth, how great an honor it is esteemed to serve under them. If therefore the soldier of the king ought to endure hardness, not to endure hardness is not the part of any soldier. So that it behooves thee not to complain, if thou endurest hardness, for that is the part of a soldier; but to complain, if thou dost not endure hardness.
